title: 4GE1-style exam questions: Water use, quality and supply (1.3)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 55 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 55: Water use, quality and supply (1.3). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Evaluate the use of reservoirs to increase water supply.' Plan, then write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Advantages: large reliable store, HEP, flood control, recreation; disadvantages: cost, flooding land and homes, ecosystems, evaporation, sediment trapped; substantiated judgement
questions.model: Teacher plans: intro defines reservoirs; P1 advantages with example (Kielder); P2 disadvantages; P3 alternatives; conclusion: worthwhile where managed carefully, with a reason.

questions.q: Compare desalination and water transfer as ways to meet a deficit.
questions.a: Desalination: unlimited, energy-hungry, costly; transfer: uses existing surplus, costly infrastructure and environmental impacts; comparison words used

questions.q: How can individuals reduce water demand?
questions.a: Shorter showers, fixing leaks, water meters, reusing water (any two)

questions.q: Explain why south-east England has a water deficit.
questions.a: Lower rainfall than the north and west (1); high population density and demand (1); so demand exceeds supply (1)
questions.model: Supply side: less rain falls in the south-east. Demand side: many people and businesses. Put together: demand is greater than supply: a deficit.

questions.a: Taking water from rivers or groundwater

questions.q: Suggest one cause of poor water quality.
questions.a: For example: fertiliser runoff, sewage or industrial pollution

questions.q: Big question: why does the wettest part of the UK not need the most water?
questions.a: The wettest areas have fewer people; demand is highest in the drier, crowded south-east
